_about: Chapter 1 (prototype) lesson order: Grandma's house. Tess and Lina approved. One room per lesson as Grandma recovers. Each lesson lists its practice words: real words, which will come with a picture and audio. Titles marked null are for Tess to write.
_why_this_order: ㅂ builds on ㅁ (the same closed lips, plus a puff); ㅂ and ㄱ unlock most household words; ㄹ is the hardest to say, so it comes last.

lessons.title: The three strokes
teaches: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ built from the strokes
tall vowels stand to the right, flat vowels lie underneath
ㄱ: k-like at the start, g-like between vowels
final consonants ㅁ ㄴ ㅇ ㅂ ㄱ
ㅇ is silent at the start, 'ng' at the end
lessons.audio_note: TTS is unreliable on isolated syllables like 앙. Check every clip by ear or use native recordings.

lessons.title: The lost boy at the gate
lessons.story: A boy is lost at the gate looking for his 누나. Her younger female friend calls her 언니. The rule: the speaker's gender and who is older decide the word; both are also used for older friends.
lessons.order_notes: Casual 응/아니 only; polite 네/아니요 come in the base game with ㅐ ㅔ. The player's own kinship choice starts with townsperson #2.

teaches: ㄹ: a flap between vowels, l at the end

base_game_later: L8: y-vowels ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ
L10: ㅐ and ㅔ taught as one sound

review.counts_as_review: first attempt only, recall formats only (typing or building)

end_check._status: From the old order; Tess to update for L1-L7 (네/아니요 and some words are now base game).
parts: Type 10 unseen syllables from audio, including nonsense syllables
Match heard words to pictures: 나/너, 문/눈, 오이/아이
Answer heard yes/no questions with 네/아니요
Say which word a boy uses and which a girl uses (누나/언니)
end_check.delayed_probe: 2 minutes, 8 random words, at next launch a day or more later; drives the progress meter
